Main question: How do computers communicate over a network?

---
 Let's start with the question - What is a computer network? 
# What is a computer network?
> A computer network is a communications medium. That's all. Nothing more. A "computer" can be digital, analog, or organic in the form of people which is where the term "computer" was first applied, that is to "one who calculates". In that sense a "computer network" can be verbal, nonverbal, analog, digital... etc, etc.
> - b4xt3r from [a reddit post](https://www.reddit.com/r/InformationTechnology/comments/efqch1/serious_question_what_exactly_is_a_computer/)

I like this particular idea of a computer network because it's more generally accurate.

So the basic idea of a computer network is that it's a communication medium that allows two or more computers to exchange data.

Now let's say you wish to send a meme to your friend and a work-related report to your colleague form your computer, how do you/your computer know which computer belongs to your friend and should be sent the meme and which computer belongs to your colleague and should be sent the report? How does a computer know what, where, or who the other computer is? 

- How does a computer know exactly which computer to send the data to?

From what I know, IP address is used to uniquely identify devices over a network.


# IP Address
IP stands for Internet Protocol.

>An Internet Protocol address (IP address) is a numerical label, such as 192.168.1.1 or 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334, that is assigned to a device connected to a computer network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication.
> - [Wikipedia - IP Address](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IP_address)

- What is the Internet Protocol?
- Who assigns the IP address to a device?

## Internet Protocol

> The Internet Protocol (IP) is a protocol, or set of rules, for routing and addressing packets of data so that they can travel across networks and arrive at the correct destination. Data traversing the Internet is divided into smaller pieces, called packets. IP information is attached to each packet, and this information helps routers to send packets to the right place. Every device or domain that connects to the Internet is assigned an IP address, and as packets are directed to the IP address attached to them, data arrives where it is needed.
> - [Cloudflare - What is the Internet Protocol?](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/network-layer/internet-protocol/)

Autology - study of self
I'll be noting down things I know about myself and problems about myself that I need to work on or answers I need to figure out.

# Shoulder joint
- Makes clicking sound as if the joint moved and snapped back into position whenever I rotate my shoulder.
- Not necessarily painful but is slightly uncomfortable.

# Intense craving for sweet
The craving is what I'd assume the closest feeling to addiction I have.
I don't even crave cigarettes as much when I stop all of a sudden after a while.
The craving of sweet almost always wins. Sometimes it gets so intense that I can't think straight without acting on it. It makes me desperate to eat something sweet. Stopping cigarettes doesn't even feel close to this kind of desperation or foggy mind I get from craving sweet at times.
If I have something sweet in my daily schedule, I've have to have it everyday around the same time in my schedule. But on the other hand if I slowly reduce the amount of sugar then eventually stop entirely, I manage to go on without having any sweets and that goes on for days, months even. Until I "relapse" I suppose after having sweets again at some point.

Had that intense craving for sweet again earlier today. Ate a lot of jaggery followed by shikran (milk + sugar + banana pieces in it). The jaggery itself was already too much sweet and yet it couldn't satisfy or calm me.

# Lack of anger/rage
It's not that I never get angry or annoyed. I feel like I've suppressed this feeling so much for so long that I don't feel it the way I should in situations that warrants anger. I let things go too much too easily. Don't get angry at things that should be getting me angry. Dealing with the anger or angry situations in a rational manner and being able to not make stupid decisions in anger and instead communicate clearly is different than just not feeling anger in a situation that warrants anger. I feel like I'm avoiding the feeling rather than dealing with it.
Makes me wonder if I really ever overcame being a people pleaser or that it just manifests itself in a different form now. Highly likely that it could be the latter.

# Lack of precise motor control
I have previously mentioned this somewhere but I feel like my motor control has declined over the years. I no longer feel that I am being precise even while doing common day to day activities like writing or typing. Even missing my target such as a button while clicking quite often (almost every time) and sometimes having to try re-clicking multiple times just for the click to land at the correct location. However, just now, I was trying to draw free hand circles using a pen and a notebook and my handwriting after that felt cleaner compared to before. I also felt in more control of my strokes. My initial hypothesis is - drawing circles is something that I'm not used to. Doing something that I'm not commonly used to made my brain work, put in some actual effort. Kind of like activating my brain rather than just working in autopilot mode as it has been for many years now. In turn allowing better control over my movement.

Still doesn't explain the degradation of precise motor control though. Although I'm not even sure if my motor control even has actually deteriorated in the first place or I'm just falsely assuming that it has.
